name: Victorian trademark
summary: A pictorial trademark from the age of the first trademark registers. A figure, an animal or a scene sits in an oval or a cartouche, with engraved line shading, banners and three or more typefaces on one label.

philosophy.core_thesis: A mark earns trust when it shows a rich, finished picture and the full name of the maker, so the buyer sees the cost and the care behind the goods.
design_principles: Put a pictorial device at the centre: an animal, a figure or an object, at 50–70% of the label height.
Close the device in an oval, a circle or a cartouche, with a border band 6–10% of the mark width.
Shade with engraved hatch lines at 0.3–0.6 mm pitch in print; let 2–4 tones come from line density, not from tint.
Set the name on an arc or a ribbon banner that follows the frame, in 2–4 typefaces of different classes.
Fill the corners with scrolls, medals or rules, so that less than 20% of the area stays empty.
Print in 1–2 inks for an engraving, or in 4–8 flat stones for a chromolithograph.
anti_patterns: A single flat shape with no picture
Large empty ground around the device
One sans-serif typeface for all text
A mark that must read below 20 mm high
Gradients made by a screen or by software

construction.grid: No modular grid. A central axis and a closed oval or circle set the layout; the banners follow arcs concentric with the frame.
construction.geometry: Ovals and circles drawn with a compass for the frame; the picture and the scrolls are freehand.
construction.stroke_rule: Hairlines of about 0.5% of the mark height for hatching; frame rules and the main letter stems at 4–6%.
construction.symmetry: Mirror symmetry on the vertical axis for the frame and the banners; the picture inside may be asymmetric.
construction.detail_floor: Hatch gaps and hairlines of 0.3–0.5% of the mark height, so the mark needs a large size.

form.silhouette: An oval, a circle or a shield, from 1:1 to 4:3 wide, with ribbons that break out of the frame at the top or the bottom.
form.ornament: Scrolls, laurel, medals, rope borders and cross-hatched shadow, in the corners and around the frame.
form.letterforms: A mix of Didone capitals, slab serifs, Tuscan display letters and script; set on an arc, with tight spacing and shadowed or outlined capitals.

colour.strategy: Engraving: one dark ink on a cream paper. Chromolithograph: a deep red and a dark blue lead, with gold, cream and black.
colour.reversal_rule: A one-colour version keeps the hatch lines but drops the flat colour fields; a reversed version needs heavier hatching, at least 1.5 times the line weight.

reproduction.clear_space: 0.1 × the frame height on each side; the label edge is often the clear space.
reproduction.media: Copperplate and wood engraving, chromolithography on labels, trade cards and tins.

positive: deep red and dark blue with gold

emotion.target_response: Trust in an old, solid maker: the viewer reads the detail as proof of quality and age.

avoid_when: The mark must read as an app icon at 16–48 px.
The brief asks for a quiet, modern or technical tone.

modifiers.how: Keep the closed frame and the banner; drop the hatching and the scenes, and reduce to 2–3 flat colours.
Keep the frame and the ornament; replace the picture with interlaced initials and whiplash curves.

colour_count.note: A chromolithograph can use up to 8 inks; the domain stops at 6.

stroke_weight.note: Hatch lines are near 0.5%; the main stems are 4 to 6%.
